searchText: There was a proposal to add `getPayloadV2` with the return value extended by the diff of the fee recipient's balance before and after executing a block. We don't want to make any changes to `getPayloadV1` before the Merge Got it. This is probably what Francesco was trying to tell me, so yes I was wrong about the 5 sec PBS disadvantage. However, the wider point remains that producers have a network latency advantage over builders that aren't producers. This means that the larger a pool is, the more mev it can make than anyone else- which has bad ramifications I've had a first go at a simple model for testing whether mev auctions solve pool centralization resulting from mev extraction Early results: 1) validator centralization from mev is pretty small in all cases, even over 50 years 2) mev auctions make it worse 3) toxic mev mitigation makes it better 4) builder/order flow centralization (which is incentivized by mev auctions without toxic mev mitigation) makes things way worse Caveat: I didn't spend very long on this, so it may be utterly wrong I'd appreciate any input people might have on it Run the code in your browser: https://dotnetfiddle.net/DRPUAd My results: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1vQ8dsBoyj8TD5fGR7wd3Is_JJ7aDzktKJcQY7x7JSaE/edit?usp=sharing I think the general principle here is that if a pool is significantly better at extracting than anyone else, they will earn more to reinvest in staking by using mev auctions, hence worsening validator centralization. Builder centralization is incentivized by mev auctions, especially private order flow from users trying to avoid toxic mev, which worsens centralization further (ie: builder centralization causes validator centralization). (the builder centralization modelling is dodgy, I just added it as a fixed amount of mev for now- actually there will be a feedback effect)

excerpts.content: Got it. This is probably what Francesco was trying to tell me, so yes I was wrong about the 5 sec PBS disadvantage. However, the wider point remains that producers have a network latency advantage over builders that aren't producers. This means that the larger a pool is, the more mev it can make than anyone else- which has bad ramifications

excerpts.author: pmcgoohan
excerpts.content: I've had a first go at a simple model for testing whether mev auctions solve pool centralization resulting from mev extraction

excerpts.author: pmcgoohan
excerpts.content:
Early results:
1) validator centralization from mev is pretty small in all cases, even over 50 years
2) mev auctions make it worse
3) toxic mev mitigation makes it better
4) builder/order flow centralization (which is incentivized by mev auctions without toxic mev mitigation) makes things way worse
